correspondence.finding: The short western start descends through the drainage west of Pindobaçu, approaches the Carnaíba–Marota setting and turns southeast toward the Itapicuru-Açu corridor. The IBGE sheet distinguishes several local streams here; no exact feeder hydronym or surveyed source is assigned to the modeled starting segment.

The eastward continuation passes the Pindobaçu and Ponto Novo impoundment settings and follows the mapped Rio Itapicuru-Açu. The northward Aipim and southwestward Rio das Pedras approaches are separate contributions, not additional selected mainstems or aliases.

Below Ponto Novo, the route runs southeast and east toward Queimadas, through the Barragem do Leste setting. The basin sheet separates Itapicuru-Mirim from the southwest and Jacurici from the north. Neither tributary is substituted for the selected western approach.

The middle course continues east south of Tucano, makes the characteristic bends near Cipó, then turns southeast past the Nova Soure–Itapicuru setting toward Acajutiba. These successive bends and settlement relationships match the mapped Itapicuru trunk throughout.

The final reach turns east past the Conde setting toward the Atlantic. The basin sheet distinguishes this channel from Piranji to the north and Itariri to the south. The modeled endpoint is treated as coastal-mouth context, without fixing a surveyed mouth or tidal boundary.

The modeled beginning takes a southern lake-and-feeder approach eastward, then turns north into the eastern end of Lac Long and runs west. It does not follow the separate northern headwater branches shown on the maps; the first feeder remains unnamed.

After the westward Long passage, the route bends south and southeast through the elongated Lac Brûlé corridor, then continues south along the labeled Romaine. Long and Brûlé are lake passages, not river-name aliases; the neighboring Lac Norman branch is distinct.

The long southern reach and pronounced southwest-then-east bend match the Romaine-4 sector before continuing toward Romaine-3. Rivière Touladis enters separately from the west, while the de l’Abbé-Huard contribution enters farther downstream from the east; neither branch is followed by the selected line.

The continuation follows the Romaine-2 and Romaine-1 sectors. The 2019 map distinguishes reservoirs from river reaches and still shows Romaine-4 under construction; Hydro-Québec reported all four stations commissioned in October 2023. Older channel geometry is therefore not interpreted as current shorelines or an entirely free-flowing river.

The southern piece makes the distinctive westward turn parallel to the coast toward the Romaine mouth setting west of Havre-Saint-Pierre. The mapped Mingan River is separate. Regional correspondence does not fix the modeled endpoint to a surveyed mouth, tidal limit or individual estuarine channel.

The southwestern headward piece follows the Gran Rio approach shown beside the Eilerts de Haan mountain setting on the institutional map. Its long northeastward course matches the western of the two upper branches. The regional drawing does not name every small headmost feeder.

The selected approach joins the northward upper-river corridor, while the map shows Pikien Rio entering from the east. Pikien Rio is a separate source branch, not an alias of Gran Rio or an additional selected branch. The model-piece boundary is not treated as the hydronym transition.

The northward corridor turns northeast into the southwest side of Lake Brokopondo and continues through the waterbody toward its northern outlet. This distinct lake passage prevents interpreting the complete selected line as uninterrupted river bearing one name.
Below Brokopondo the selected trunk continues north on the mapped Suriname R. toward Paramaribo. The map separates this corridor from Saramacca R. to the west and Commewijne R. to the east.

The northern endpoint lies in the Paramaribo-area lower river, downstream of the Jules Wijdenbosch bridge but upstream of Suzannasdaal Anchorage. MAS identifies both locations on the tidal Suriname River and catalogs a Suriname River–Paramaribo chart. The selected line does not reach the open Atlantic mouth.

The western selected approach lies in the southern Chico Alto headwater arm. The glacier-inventory map separates this arm from the northern Belgrano–Roble/Lago Burmeister drainage. The initial short feeder and its precise name transition are left unassigned; the model does not traverse Lago Burmeister.

The route continues east along the mapped upper Chico valley, then turns southeast toward the Gobernador Gregores setting. The original maps distinguish the Belgrano joining corridor from the selected western approach rather than treating every source branch as one hydronym.

Around Gobernador Gregores the selected route bends south, east and south again, then takes a long southeastward course north and east of Lago Cardiel. The province map shows the same Chico corridor and keeps Cardiel in its separate drainage unit; the selection is not a through-lake Cardiel route.

The lower route turns east-southeast at the Chalía junction setting and follows the corridor directly labeled R. Chico toward the RN 3 crossing. Río Chalía or Sheuen enters separately from the west; neither its upper route nor the more southerly Río Santa Cruz trunk is substituted for the selected line.

The final southward leg approaches the northern estuarine arm near the Piedrabuena–Puerto Santa Cruz region. The map depicts the separate Santa Cruz river approaching from the west and the wider coastal inlet farther downstream. The selected endpoint is not assigned an exact tidal boundary or the full shared estuary to the Atlantic.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
